summary: Frontend-only verification of the HIGH sticky sub-nav fix on /handeln (iteration_57 defect) plus scroll-spy regression and the P0 ProductInquiryStickyCta regression on Home. HIGH FIX CONFIRMED: at 1440px the global header measures top 0..114 (sticky, z-index 100) and the sub-nav wrapper now renders at top 114..164.75 with computed top=114px, z-index=95; at 390px header 0..106 and sub-nav 106..156.75 (top=106px). After window.scrollTo(0,3000) document.elementsFromPoint() on every hub-subnav-* button center returns that same button as the topmost element (no header nodes) — 0 covered buttons on desktop; on mobile the 3 buttons inside the viewport are topmost and the remaining 4 simply lie outside the 390px viewport inside the horizontally scrollable nav (expected, not a defect). Normal (non-forced) Playwright clicks on hub-subnav-orderarten while scrolled succeed at both viewports, page scrolls so section top = ~160px and the H2 headline is the topmost element at its center (fully visible below header+sub-nav), with data-active='true'. Scroll-spy still activates exactly one matching button for all 7 sections (grundlagen, anlageklassen, orderarten, kosten, risiken, abc, fehler). Click-to-scroll for kosten/risiken/abc/fehler/grundlagen all land headline top at 280px, visible, correct active state. Deep links /handeln#kosten, #risiken, #abc (full document loads with seeded localStorage) all land with sectionTop=160, headline visible and matching button active — desktop and mobile. P0 CTA regression: all clean.

ui_bugs.issue: Carry-over LOW from iter 57 (intentionally not fixed): data-near-form attribute is only emitted on the mobile branch; desktop root returns null. Cosmetic/test-parity only.

issues: Carry-over LOW: 10.5px uppercase with 0.18em tracking is at the lower bound of legibility; inactive rgb(100,116,139) small-caps text is borderline contrast.

critical_code_review_comments: HandelnHub.jsx is 869 lines — still above the 700-line guideline; extract SECTIONS/ASSET_CLASSES/ORDER_TYPES/COSTS/RISK_POINTS/COMMON_MISTAKES data and useScrollSpy into separate modules.

Sub-nav sticky offset (top-[106px]/sm:top-[114px]) and NAV_OFFSET=160 are hard-coded duplicates of the header height defined in Navigation.js. If the header height changes, both break silently — consider a single CSS custom property (e.g. --header-h) consumed by both the sticky offset and NAV_OFFSET.

Client-side hash changes within the same document (e.g. link from /handeln#kosten to /handeln#risiken without a remount) do not re-trigger the deep-link effect (deps []), so the offset scroll is skipped and the section can land at viewport top 0 (behind the header). Only reproducible via in-document hash navigation, not on fresh loads; consider a hashchange listener if in-page hash links are added later.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested assertions passed (HIGH fix verified at 1440px and 390px; scroll-spy + deep-link + P0 sticky CTA regressions all pass)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bypass the visitor gate by setting localStorage kapitalmitte_visitor_profile and kapitalmitte_cookie_consent then page.reload(); a fresh browser context WILL show [data-testid='visitor-welcome-gate'] overlay and make elementFromPoint checks return the gate. For deep-link tests always do a real document load (goto /handeln, seed, goto /handeln#<id>, reload) — in-document hash changes do not re-run the deep-link effect and give a false sectionTop=0. Sticky sub-nav fix verified good: header 114px desktop / 106px mobile, sub-nav top-[106px]/sm:top-[114px] z-[95], NAV_OFFSET=160 places section tops exactly at the sub-nav bottom edge.
rca_of_the_issue: Iteration_57 HIGH bug (sub-nav painted under the z-100 sticky header) is resolved: the wrapper now sticks at the measured header height (114px desktop / 106px mobile) with z-95, so it sits directly below the header instead of inside its band; hit-testing returns the sub-nav buttons. NAV_OFFSET=160 (=114 header + ~46 sub-nav) keeps section headlines below both bars after scrollToId and keeps the IntersectionObserver activation band aligned.
